baseline.evidence: Agree with the self-score. A newcomer needs fold, empty/update/close of a state, strata, tails and on="items"/share explained, and the first output is the repr Collection(15 aliases over 5 states). The plain comments help, but the code still speaks the jargon.

r2-1.evidence: Every verb is Keras/torchmetrics (update, compute, reset), and every output is a dict or table with units. The gate's pass/FAIL grid over all 36 cells, with 36 of 36 and 33 of 36, is the clearest verdict in the round. Two catches. A newcomer has to know update() piles up until reset(), which is why live starts with reset(). rung_table(runs, pendulum_arm_metrics) passes the factory, not a call; its comment explains why.

r2-2.evidence: The plainest face: call a function on a run and get a number, with the unit in its name. print(metric.__doc__) explains each metric in one English line, and the gate is `stop <= gate_mm`. Weaker spots: the owner is only a comment on a bare float, and the verdict shows CAN 11's six rows, not all 36 cells.

r2-3.evidence: Reads at a glance for a pandas/Polars user, and printing a metric gives its plain definition. The pivot of the worst stop over all 36 cells is the most informative single output in the round. A non-pandas reader needs agg, pivot(on=, index=, values=), with_columns and Runs([run]) explained, and `column <= limit` compares with a Threshold object by operator overloading. Between the 3 and 5 anchors.

r2-4.evidence: Every output is a table that answers 'did it pass?' in words. print(card) reads as a spec: check, how it is measured, unit, target, owner. card.check(runs, by=...) lists the failing groups by name. Catches: the tracking-RMS target (<= 0.5, AI agent) is the agent's proposal and should be labelled 'proposed'. card.check(live) accepting a live tally is a little magic, but it reads right.
